item.text: I’ll plan a signed-in Django website with a seven-day booking window and at most two upcoming bookings per member. For the remaining choices, I’ll use hourly starts and a configurable club timezone, initially UTC, and make those assumptions explicit in the setup package.

# Review contract

Verification backends read this file: they receive it alongside the diff and are asked to name the principle a finding violates. Ordinary coding sessions do not read it.

A finding names the principle it violates. Name it and judge severity independently: the class governs blocking only, and it never lowers what you reported. A `blocking` class ADDS blocking to a finding already at critical or major severity. `major` and `suggestion` add nothing and leave your own decision untouched, so a finding the reviewer blocked on still blocks. `correctness` is a seventh value a finding may name and it blocks like security; it is the floor beneath the six, not one of them. Once capping is enabled, a finding inside this contract that names no principle is capped at suggestion.

## Outside this contract

accessibility, performance, data-safety

## Coherence

The change fits the design it lands in: one concept has one home, and new code follows the boundaries and data flow the project already has.

Violations: a second copy of an existing abstraction; logic placed in a layer the project keeps it out of; a reverse dependency between modules; a suggested ruling that applies and is not cited.

Blocking: major

## Uniformity

Same things look the same: naming, error shapes, file layout, and interfaces match the project's existing patterns.

Violations: a new naming scheme beside the existing one; an error returned where the project throws; a hand-rolled utility where a shared one exists.

Blocking: major

## Maintainability

The next reader can change it safely: intent is stated where it is not obvious, and the change is no larger or more coupled than its job requires.

Violations: a load-bearing decision with no recorded reason; a function that needs the whole file read to be changed; dead or duplicated paths left behind.

Blocking: major

## Robustness

The code behaves under the inputs and failures it will actually meet: bounds, absence, concurrency, partial failure, restart.

Violations: an unbounded read or loop; an absent value treated as zero; a write with no durability barrier where one is expected; a resource not released on the failure path.

Blocking: blocking

## Security

No new way for untrusted input or a less trusted party to act with more authority than intended.

Violations: unvalidated external input reaching a command, query, path, or privileged call; secrets or credentials in code or logs; a permission or sandbox setting widened without an explicit decision.

Blocking: blocking

## Quality

The change is verified to do what it claims: tests exist for the behaviour, they fail without the change, and the claim in the description matches what shipped.

Violations: a test that passes with the change removed; a green suite over code that is never executed; a description that names work the diff does not contain; a grep transcript in EXISTING.

Blocking: major

## Notes on this file

Ordering is load-bearing. The lens backend receives only the first 3000 characters of this file, head-truncated, so the six principles stay above anything this project adds. A principle pushed below that line is one a lens reviewer is asked to name without ever being shown it.

The "Outside this contract" line is read literally. Every line under that heading is split on commas and newlines into entries, trailing punctuation is stripped, and a `- ` bullet prefix is NOT stripped, so a bulleted entry matches nothing and prose written there becomes junk entries. One plain comma-separated line, or nothing at all. Entries are matched against a finding's category and, for a merged lens finding, against every contributing lens id.

A finding outside the contract is never capped and keeps the severity its reviewer gave it. Outside is therefore the LOUD side: the shorter the line, the more this contract covers and the more it quiets. An empty line is the widest coverage and the quietest gate, which is why `storybloq validate` warns about one. Silencing a category is a different mechanism and lives in `.story/config.json` under `recipeOverrides.blockingPolicy.neverBlock`.

The Outside line ships with three lens ids on it because the six principles above genuinely say nothing
about those subjects, and a finding is better passed through on its reviewer's judgement than capped for
naming no principle. Remove an entry to bring that subject under the contract; add one, as a category
string or a lens id, to take a subject out. Do not use this line to silence a category: a finding outside
the contract keeps the severity its reviewer gave it, which is louder, not quieter. Silencing lives in
`.story/config.json` under `recipeOverrides.blockingPolicy.neverBlock`.

Review this proposed Storybloq setup plan independently for coverage, fidelity, journey completeness, boundaries/dependencies, feasibility, safety and acceptance evidence. Return only schema-shaped verdict and findings. No writes or execution of tests/install/build/server.
Sources: README.md says tennis club has three courts; members book one-hour slots, never double-book a court/slot, cancel until two hours before start; guest payments later. Owner conversation: about 80 members with individual club accounts; booking up to seven days ahead; at most two upcoming bookings; retain Django; other choices delegated to judgement.
Existing code: Booking(court positive small integer, starts_at datetime, member charfield), UniqueConstraint court+starts_at. No migrations, URLs/views/templates or cancellation. Django auth installed, SQLite, USE_TZ true. requirements Django/pytest/pytest-django. Makefile test runs pytest, README says make test, pytest.ini collects tests.py and test_*.py and sets club.settings; bookings/tests.py exists. No git. No completion claims for unevidenced functionality.
Project: Court bookings; generic Python/Django. Existing model recorded as baseline in handover, no complete tickets.
Assumptions: server-rendered Django site, staff-provisioned Django accounts with admin password reset, no public signup; UTC club timezone initially configurable before real use; court IDs 1..3; starts on local clock hour, exactly one elapsed hour; eligible start strictly future and <= now+7*24h; upcoming means active start>now; cancellation allowed at exactly two hours remaining and denied below, enforced server-side; own bookings only; canceled slots reusable, preserve cancellation record. No opening-hour restrictions requested, show every valid hourly slot. DST ambiguous/nonexistent local hours handled explicitly with offset labels and UTC uniqueness. SQLite retained initially, database-level serialized write strategy and real concurrency tests, no reliance on ineffective row locks.
First version excludes payments, guests, public signup, notifications, recurring bookings, public deployment automation. Accounts must be usable and staff password reset documented; production settings/hardening and staff setup documented before real deployment, no public deployment as part of setup.
Milestones after default p0:
p1 Accounts and booking interaction preview
p2 Safe booking and cancellation
p3 Integrated member experience and acceptance
All task descriptions below use required template. References A..I provisional IDs.
A p1 Club accounts and runnable Django foundation
Outcome: each member signs in with own account (owner conversation).
Scope: URL/settings/template wiring, Django session login/logout, staff admin provisioning and password reset, migrations and auth ownership for Booking with explicit safe handling of legacy free-text members. Excludes: public registration.
Acceptance: two accounts login independently, anonymous requests redirect, authenticated member resolved server-side, CSRF on mutations, admin-only account management; existing free-text bookings require explicit mapping and unresolved rows block migration rather than guessed ownership; clean DB setup succeeds.
Behaviour: accessible labelled forms, generic invalid login errors, safe logout, unauthorized access denied; no silent legacy data loss.
Verification: make test for auth, access, migration clean/legacy mapping and rollback; documented local setup. Prerequisites: none. Assumptions: staff provisions accounts; no evidence of deployed data.
B p1 Booking interaction preview
Outcome: owner sees availability, booking errors, my bookings and cancel cutoff (README and owner).
Scope: accessible server-rendered static/demo states for three courts and seven-day navigation with explicit UTC labels. Excludes: booking persistence.
Acceptance: keyboard-usable preview shows free/occupied slots, quota reached, empty bookings and cancel unavailable; no other member names exposed.
Behaviour: labels, focus/error summaries, status feedback; explicit demo data.
Verification: template tests via make test and owner inspection. Prerequisites: A. Assumptions: server-rendered forms, hourly slots.
C p1 Checkpoint: member booking flow and timezone
Question: Is the preview understandable and is UTC the right initial club timezone?
Artifact: B screens and explicit rules/timezone assumptions.
Criteria: owner inspects states and timezone; any change recorded. Prerequisites: B. Follow-on affected: G, not booking core D/E/F which uses configurable timezone.
D p2 Court slots and booking persistence
Outcome: book valid one-hour court slots with no duplicate active slot (README).
Scope: court bounds, aligned aware start, configurable timezone, seven-day boundary, active/canceled record status, migrations/unique active-slot constraint and atomic single-slot write service. Excludes: member quota (E), public booking endpoint (G).
Acceptance: reject bad court, past/unaligned/out-of-window start; exactly seven days allowed; simultaneous same-slot requests yield one booking; DST gaps/ambiguity explicit; canceled slot reusable.
Behaviour: validation and conflict errors actionable, rollback partial writes, no member identity accepted from client.
Verification: make test with DB constraint, time boundaries, DST and concurrency tests against SQLite file DB. Prerequisites: A. Assumptions: all hours offered, calendar display club timezone, seven days means rolling 168 hours.
E p2 Two-upcoming-booking limit
Outcome: member never holds more than two upcoming bookings (owner).
Scope: transactionally enforce quota alongside D booking write, count active future starts, serialize concurrent creates/cancels through SQLite-supported write strategy with bounded contention handling. Excludes: UI.
Acceptance: third denied; past/canceled bookings not counted; concurrent different-slot requests for same member cannot exceed two; both quota and slot rules maintained.
Behaviour: quota/conflict feedback, rollback on failure; lock contention retry bounded and fails safely.
Verification: make test boundary/count and real independent DB-connection concurrency regression tests; document DB semantics, do not rely on select_for_update in SQLite. Prerequisites: D. Assumptions: no overlap restriction beyond explicit quota.
F p2 Own-booking cancellation
Outcome: owner can cancel own booking with at least two hours left (README).
Scope: authorized transactional cancellation service using same write serialization; preserve record, release slot/quota. Excludes: staff policy overrides and UI.
Acceptance: exactly two hours allowed, under two denied; other member cannot cancel; repeated cancel safe; concurrent cancel/create preserves slot and quota.
Behaviour: clear late/unauthorized errors without leaking member details; timezone-aware clock, safe repeat requests.
Verification: make test boundary, authorization, reuse and race tests. Prerequisites: E. Assumptions: inclusive cutoff.
G p3 Live availability and member bookings
Outcome: signed-in member chooses court/time, books and cancels, sees own upcoming bookings (README/owner).
Scope: wire preview to D/E/F services, seven-day availability, POST forms, CSRF, refresh availability after conflicts, own bookings page. Excludes: other-member details and deferred features.
Acceptance: full journey succeeds; occupied and quota states clear; stale slot cannot duplicate; cancellations update availability; server enforces all rules even forged requests.
Behaviour: accessible errors/focus, empty states, feedback, pending submission affordance where relevant, safe repeat submissions, club timezone labels.
Verification: make test Django client journey/security tests and keyboard browser walkthrough. Prerequisites: C,E,F. Assumptions: forms, no SPA.
H p3 Acceptance evidence and operating guide
Outcome: staff can provision ~80 individual accounts and run/verify the first version.
Scope: combined acceptance suite, staff account/timezone setup guide, backup/restore smoke procedure, production configuration checklist (secret outside repo, debug off, allowed hosts, HTTPS/secure cookies), establish supported server start/readiness command. Excludes: public deployment execution, load target invention.
Acceptance: matrix covers every booking/auth rule and failure, concurrent quota/slot evidence, setup from clean DB, owner can repeat demo with two accounts; security settings documented before real use.
Behaviour: recovery instructions for conflict/lock contention/migration mapping, no secrets in docs.
Verification: make test integrated regression; manual documented restore and keyboard walkthrough during implementation, not setup. Prerequisites: G. Assumptions: deployment target undecided and not required for local first version.
I p3 Checkpoint: first-version acceptance
Criteria: owner demonstrates individual login, three courts/hour slots, seven-day boundary, two-upcoming cap, no duplicate under race, own cancellation at/below cutoff, access/privacy and agreed timezone.
Artifact: running site and H evidence. Prerequisites: H.
Checkpoints are ordinary tickets, not enforced gates; only dependent work waits.
Coverage: individual accounts/80 members=A,H; three courts/hour/no-double=D,G,H; seven days=D,G; two upcoming=E,G; cancel cutoff/ownership=F,G; Django=A..H; payments deferred; delegated UX/timezone=A,B,C,D,G; acceptance=I.
Governance proposal: create AGENTS.md purpose/stack/architecture/assumptions/testing, RULES.md invariants/security/TDD for business logic, REVIEW.md exact skill review contract template. Git init, .gitignore Storybloq runtime paths plus Python caches, .venv, local SQLite and environment secret files. No GitHub import.
Quality level: Full pipeline because business rules/workflow. WRITE_TESTS enabled command make test, TEST enabled make test (established by Makefile/README+collected tests.py). BUILD disabled no manifest build command. VERIFY disabled pending runnable server wiring and readiness endpoint; proposed python manage.py runserver 127.0.0.1:8000 with http://127.0.0.1:8000/accounts/login/ after A/H implementation, not established from manifest now. No tests/install/build/server run during setup.
Create init/phases/tickets/dependencies/config/governance/gitignore/git baseline snapshot/setup note/initial handover only after setup package approval. No app implementation as part of setup.

STORYBLOQ_PLAN"

item.text:
The proposed setup tracks a Django website where roughly 80 members sign in, book one-hour slots on three courts up to seven days ahead, hold at most two upcoming bookings, and cancel their own bookings until two hours before the start. Guest payments remain deferred.

I’ve chosen staff-created accounts, hourly starts, and a configurable club timezone initially set to UTC. The seven-day window means a rolling 168 hours; cancellation is allowed at exactly the two-hour cutoff.

Phases are milestones; tickets are specific work items within them. The proposed inventory uses temporary labels until Storybloq assigns IDs:

| Milestone | Ticket and purpose | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| Accounts and preview | **A:** Individual accounts, login/logout, Django wiring, safe booking ownership migration | — |
| | **B:** Accessible preview of availability, booking limits, and cancellation states | A |
| | **C:** Checkpoint: inspect the member journey and timezone display | B |
| Safe booking | **D:** Valid court/hour slots, seven-day boundary, persistent double-booking prevention | A |
| | **E:** Enforce the two-upcoming-booking limit, including simultaneous requests | D |
| | **F:** Authorized cancellation, cutoff enforcement, slot and quota release | E |
| Member experience | **G:** Connect availability, booking, and cancellation screens to the validated services | C, E, F |
| | **H:** Integrated acceptance tests and staff operating/recovery guide | G |
| | **I:** Checkpoint: demonstrate and accept the first version | H |

Ticket A can begin immediately after setup. Checkpoints are ordinary tickets with dependencies; Storybloq does not yet enforce owner approval before they can be closed.

Approval covers **Court bookings**, a Python/Django project: the default setup phase plus these three milestones, nine tickets, their dependencies, a baseline snapshot, setup note, and initial handover. It also covers creating `AGENTS.md`, `RULES.md`, and the skill’s standard `REVIEW.md` contract; initializing Git; and ignoring Storybloq runtime files, Python caches, virtual environments, local databases, and secret environment files. File previews and full ticket descriptions are available through “Inspect details.”

Quality level: Full pipeline, because booking rules and concurrent requests need verification.

| Stage | Proposed command | Status |
|---|---|---|
| WRITE_TESTS | `make test` | Established; enabled |
| TEST | `make test` | Established; enabled |
| BUILD | None | Disabled; no build command |
| VERIFY | `python manage.py runserver 127.0.0.1:8000` | Pending runnable routes/readiness; disabled |

The review clarification is incorporated: availability must include every eligible slot through the rolling window, which can span eight calendar dates. No tests or server were run during setup planning.
